chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade every intoxicant, so every intoxicant is prohibited. I said to him, 'And what about the containers from which it is made?' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the dubba', the muzaffat, the huntam, and the naqir.' I said, 'And what is that?' He said: 'The dubba is the gourd, and the muzaffat is the bitumen-coated vessel, and the huntam are green clay urns, and the naqir are wood which the people of the Pre-Islamic period used to hollow out until they became hollow vessels in which they would ferment Nabidh.'

key_terms.الدُّبَّاء: A container made from a gourd

ai.seo_question: What are the specific types of containers forbidden for making Nabidh in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the prohibition of Nabidh by linking the impurity of the drink to the specific materials of its container, a key principle in Shia fiqh regarding 'illat al-hukm' (the cause of the ruling). The four named vessels—dubba, muzaffat, huntam, and naqir—represent pre-Islamic practices that the Prophet (saww) sought to eradicate, emphasizing that the container's material directly influences the beverage's status. This establishes a practical legal framework where the prohibition extends beyond the substance itself to the means of its production.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Khalid Bin Jareer, from Abu Al Rabie Al Shamy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww forbade from every intoxicant, therefore every intoxicant is Prohibited’. So I said to himasws, ‘So (what about) the container in which it is made from?’ So heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww forbade from the pumpkin, and the asphalted pot, and the clay, and the date husk’. I said, ‘And what is that?’ Heasws said: ‘The pumpkin is the gourd, and the bitumen coated vessel, and the green clay urns, and the dry date husks which the people of the Pre-Islamic period used to make until there came to be for these a hollowness to ferment Nabeez in it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from abu al-Rabi’ al-Shamiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited all intoxicating substances, thus, all intoxicating substances are unlawful for consumption.

I then asked about utensils in which such things are made. He (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah prohibited the use of pumpkins as pots (used in fermentation of raw material for liquor), al-Danan, casks (a large container coated with asphalt), containers of pottery and palm tree trunks (curved as a container used in fermentation of raw material for intoxicating substances) in the time of ignorance before Islam.’”
